findings.title: Core random-files lesson is incorrectly labelled support-only
evidence: BILINGUAL_PARITY.json marks all 10 random-files blocks support_only=true.
DISPOSITIONS.json includes its four assessment requirements and three blocks as support-only dispositions.
findings.impact: This changes the pedagogical role and falsely communicates that a core Paper 4 lesson is optional support. It can also hide intended conceptual coverage even though no Stage 5 executable pattern is assigned to the lesson.
findings.required_fix: Classify support_only from Stage 3 scope.role, so only performance and graphs are support-only. Keep random-files as core conceptual/non-executable content and account for its requirements using an explicit non-code/core disposition or a proper Stage 5 pattern join if Lead confirms one. Regenerate skeleton, parity, dispositions, coverage and summary, then rerun A8.
findings.recheck: python -I -B build_s6f.py; independently verify random-files support_only=false, no fabricated pattern IDs, and all 4 random-files requirements remain accounted.

findings.title: Core exceptions lesson is also inferred as support-only by the same rule
evidence: Stage 3 lesson ac-9618-p4-2026-python.lesson.exceptions has scope.role=core and package_id=ac-9618-p4-2026-python.package.files, but the S6-F manifest and dispositions classify it as support-only.
findings.impact: The same role classification defect affects another core lesson and would propagate to Stage 7 handoff.
findings.required_fix: Apply the same role-aware classification to exceptions. Preserve explicit non-code disposition if no Stage 5 executable pattern is assigned; do not fabricate coverage.
findings.recheck: Verify exceptions support_only=false and its four requirements remain exactly once in the corrected matrix.
